issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - путь подытожили весь. Роза Муда - делать нам нечего здесь.
issues.translation_quote: Rosamunde - our whole road's been summed up.
issues.justification: The song is a Soviet-era parody of 'Rosamunde' (Roza Muda, a pseudo-German/French nonsense text). The translation renders it as 'Rosamunde' and then supplies real German lyrics, losing the macaronic joke and the Russian military-march text; the lyric mix is inconsistent.

issues.source_quote: Роза Муда - шент мир дер херц унд дер я. Роза Муда - франк ду них мерт ди мама. Роза Муда - глауб мир аргер детрай.
issues.translation_quote: Rosamunde - schenk mir dein Herz und sag ja. Rosamunde - frag doch nicht erst die Mama. Rosamunde - glaub mir, auch ich bin dir treu.
issues.justification: The source deliberately gives garbled phonetic pseudo-German (a Russian approximation by a singer who doesn't know German). The translation 'corrects' it into fluent German, destroying the comic gibberish effect.

issues.source_quote: Когда я на почте служил ямщиком, был молод, имел я селёдку! Селедку имел!
issues.translation_quote: I had mussels! I had mussels!
issues.justification: Soyev's verse is a bad-poetry parody of the folk song 'Когда я на почте служил ямщиком, был молод, имел я силёнку'; 'селёдку' (herring) is the comic malapropism. 'Mussels' invents a different item and no clear joke. The setup (the nonsensical slip) is lost.

issues.translation_quote: There lay, brothers, the Cold War.
issues.justification: Parodic rhyme is lost, and 'Cold War' is an anachronistic/overly specific addition; the original is 'cold war' as an image of a corpse under the seat. Also the 'Bony, toothless, without brows' verse loses meter/rhyme.

issues.source_quote: Гравировать имена победителей - работа, требующая самоотречения.
issues.translation_quote: I don't know, Lyova, about self-renunciation, that work doesn't need any finesse. It's done with a spitzstichel.
issues.justification: The dialogue about штихель types is translated inconsistently: 'спицштихель'/'вольштихель' appear as 'spitzstichel'/'vollstichel' (and 'gravers' elsewhere), with 'Одно дело...' phrasing flattened; the technical jokes about craftsmanship are muddled. Also 'Hund begraben' explanation is garbled.

issues.source_quote: Мон папа, не же па, ке же дансе, ке же дансе!
issues.translation_quote: Mon papa ne veut pas que je danse, que je danse!
issues.justification: The source is deliberately Russian-mangled French ('не же па'); correcting it to proper French loses the comic phonetics, and the later exchange 'Нё же па! / Нё жё па?' is rendered as 'Ne veut pas! / Ne vœ pas?', which no longer makes sense as a mishearing.

issues.source_quote: Они вас, Алиса Витальевна, ... Он ломает, я чиню.
issues.translation_quote: So I look after him like a child. He breaks, I fix.
issues.justification: Minor register shift aside, the preceding speech '...ну и ловок же ты сверхъестественно' is rendered 'supernaturally slick' which changes meaning (skillful, smooth operator) awkwardly; 'Scattered a home hearth to dust' is calqued.

issues.translation_quote: Culinarian!
issues.justification: Alisa's affectionate-teasing form of address to Savva is rendered with an unnatural coinage that doesn't convey the tone.

issues.source_quote: Вы - кандидат? Вы давно уже мастер. Ох, вы и мастер.
issues.translation_quote: You, a candidate? You've long been a master. Oh, what a master you are.
issues.justification: Chess pun (кандидат в мастера) plus innuendo 'мастер' (seducer) is not made clear; 'master' loses the double entendre of 'one who plays love simultaneously'.

issues.translation_quote: Émile Zola died of fumes.
issues.justification: 'Угорел' here is a tongue-in-cheek reference to Zola's real death from carbon monoxide; the later 'turn off the burners' needs a connection, but 'died of fumes' reads awkwardly; ok but also 'угорел' can mean 'went crazy'. The deadpan, joking tone is flattened.

issues.translation_quote: They've found the skull of Oleg the Wise's horse.
issues.justification: Вещий Олег is conventionally 'Oleg the Prophetic' / 'Prophetic Oleg'; 'the Wise' is a mistranslation. The reference to Pushkin's ballad is lost.

issues.translation_quote: so that your brushes are like leaves
issues.justification: Opening song lines about 'забытой городской традиции' etc. lose rhythm; the translation is prosaic and not singable, though acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Зер гут / Данке шён / Фюнф минут / Яволь / Швапс тринкен
issues.translation_quote: Schnaps trinken
issues.justification: Savva's mock-German tic is retained in some places but 'Швапс' (deliberately corrupted) and other cases are corrected, making the character voice inconsistent.

issues.translation_quote: Auf Wiedergucken
issues.justification: Acceptable pun, but 'Оревуар' etc. mix; fine.

issues.source_quote: Вы, как судьи, нарисуйте наши судьбы
issues.translation_quote: Like judges, paint our destinies
issues.justification: 'Что гадать нам удалось, не удалось' rendered 'what we managed to foresee, and what we didn't' is vague; guessing/divination sense is weakened.

issues.translation_quote: Sing, swallow, sing.
issues.justification: Velyurov's pompous satirical doggerel loses its rhyme and bureaucratic-propaganda feel; reads flat.

issues.source_quote: Был я конкурсе я джазов, обалдел от джазов сразу. Буги-вуги, самба-мамба, чувствую, приходит амба.
issues.translation_quote: At a jazz contest I was crazed, by the jazz I was amazed.
issues.justification: Rhyme is preserved but 'амба' (the end/finish) becomes 'caramba', an invention, and 'Тунеядца хоронили' lines lose the sharp parody.

issues.source_quote: Нет, моя радость, я его отчим.
issues.translation_quote: No, my joy, I'm his stepfather.
issues.justification: 'My joy' is a literal rendering of 'моя радость'; unnatural in English.

issues.source_quote: Какой он тебе пасынок? Тоже нашел себе дурочку с переулочка.
issues.translation_quote: How's he your stepson? Found himself some dimwit off the street.
issues.justification: Slightly off: 'дурочка с переулочка' is a colloquial idiom for a gullible fool, and the speaker is addressing Sveta in an aside; tone is acceptable but loses rhyme.

issues.translation_quote: "Losing mind."
issues.justification: Telegram wording is ungrammatical; a more natural 'Going out of my mind' is needed.

issues.translation_quote: I'm a candidate master.
issues.justification: Official chess/sports title; 'candidate master' is acceptable but later joke is lost.

issues.translation_quote: Khobotov, that's petty.
issues.justification: Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Вы популярны. Нет, это витаминизация популярна, не я...
issues.translation_quote: You're popular. No, it's vitamin shots that are popular, not me...
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: You're a servant of the muses. I serve Mosestrada.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: This is some kind of Paleolithic!
issues.justification: Unnatural; 'This is the Stone Age!' would be more natural.

issues.translation_quote: setzen Sie sich bitte!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Popova, Popova, Popova!
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: You bring girls over
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: a man of goodwill
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Ну на то лед, чтобы скользить.
issues.translation_quote: Well, ice is there for slipping.
issues.justification: Wordplay on 'скользкий путь' is retained; minor awkwardness.

issues.translation_quote: my friend, the tireless Sovransky
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Shoo, get out.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: He's really going at it.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Велюров, мы с тетей чистые люди
issues.translation_quote: my aunt and I are pure people
issues.justification: Calque; 'decent people' would be more natural.

issues.translation_quote: Trading in flesh?
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.translation_quote: Tartuffe.
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Вонзил кинжал убийца нечестивый в грудь деларю. Тот, шляпу сняв, сказал ему учтиво: благодарю!
issues.translation_quote: The impious killer plunged his dagger into the breast of Delarue. He doffed his hat and said politely: "Thank you!"
issues.justification: The comic rhyme деларю/благодарю is lost. The joke also turns on "деларю" (a word the verse plays with), but the translation invents a proper name, "Delarue", so the absurd humor is not recreated.

issues.source_quote: Хотя, согласись, что твое состояние от холодного далеко.
issues.translation_quote: Though you must admit, your state is far from cool-headed.
issues.justification: This is a pun on the medical term "холодная операция" (an elective operation performed in a calm period). The translation turns it into "cool-headed" and loses the medical wordplay and the sense that he is in an acute state.

issues.source_quote: Я вас люблю, хоть я бешусь, Хоть это труд и стыд напрасный.
issues.translation_quote: I love you, though it makes me rage, though it's vain toil and shame.
issues.justification: This is a Pushkin quotation. The elevated poetic register, meter and rhyme are lost, and the lines read as stilted prose.

issues.source_quote: Без вас мне скучно, я зеваю. При вас мне грустно, я терплю.
issues.translation_quote: Without you I'm bored, I yawn. With you I'm sad, I endure.
issues.justification: The rhymed Pushkin verse is rendered as flat prose, losing the poetic effect that is contrasted with the characters' banter.

issues.source_quote: постарайся произвести на моих родителей благоприятное впечатление
issues.translation_quote: try to make on my parents a favorable impression
issues.justification: Unnatural word order and stiff phrasing; natural English would be "try to make a good impression on my parents".

issues.translation_quote: You don't say it sincerely.
issues.justification: Awkward; a natural rendering would be "You're not being sincere."

issues.translation_quote: I look like some kind of dandy.
issues.justification: "Стиляга" is a specific 1950s Soviet subculture and period term. "Dandy" loses the era-specific flavor.

issues.translation_quote: the Pokrov Gate
issues.justification: The established English form is "Pokrovsky Gate(s)", which is also the film's title. "Pokrov Gate" is inaccurate and inconsistent with it.

issues.source_quote: Жить у нее, как за пазухой!
issues.translation_quote: You could live with her like in God's pocket!
issues.justification: "God's pocket" is not an English idiom and sounds odd. The sense is "snug as a bug" or "in the lap of luxury".

issues.translation_quote: They don't marry off lunatics!
issues.justification: The reference is to the official registration of marriage. "Marry off" shifts the meaning and loses the bureaucratic joke.

issues.source_quote: Тебя просил я быть на свидании
issues.translation_quote: I asked you to meet me for a date
issues.justification: Redundant and clumsy, and it does not read as natural song or verse.
